faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know about our platform
faq.question1: How does the free trial work?
faq.answer1: Start with our Free Starter plan immediately. Upgrade to paid plans anytime with a 14-day free trial. No credit card required to start.
faq.question2: Can I accept payments in Ethiopian Birr?
faq.answer2: Yes! We support TeleBirr, Chapa, and M-PESA for local Ethiopian Birr payments, plus international options like Stripe and PayPal.
faq.question3: Do my customers need to download an app?
faq.answer3: No. Customers can book via your personalized booking link in any web browser, SMS, or USSD. No app download required.
faq.answer4: Customers text your booking number, and our system guides them through available slots and confirms their appointment automatically.
faq.answer5: Yes! Business and Enterprise plans support multiple locations with separate calendars, staff, and availability for each location.
faq.question6: Is my data secure and compliant with Ethiopian law?
faq.answer6: Absolutely. We comply with Ethiopia's Personal Data Protection Proclamation 1321/2024 with bank-grade encryption and secure data storage.
faq.question7: What happens if I exceed my plan limits?
faq.answer7: We'll notify you and help you upgrade. Your service continues uninterrupted, and you only pay for what you use.
faq.question8: Do you offer support in Amharic?
faq.answer8: Yes! Our platform and customer support are available in both English and Amharic.

timeConverter.name: Ethiopian time converter
timeConverter.summary: Habesha clock to international time and back, with a 24-hour chart.
timeConverter.title: Ethiopian Time Converter: Habesha Clock to EAT
timeConverter.description: Convert Ethiopian (Habesha) time to international time and back. Free, instant and works on your phone, with a full 24-hour table and AM/PM labels.
timeConverter.lede: Convert Ethiopian (Habesha) time to international time (East Africa Time) and back. Habesha clock hours start at sunrise, so 6:00 AM is 12 o'clock (ጠዋት 12 ሰዓት).
timeConverter.rule: Habesha hour = international hour − 6, on a 12-hour clock. Minutes do not change. The day (ቀን) runs from 6:00 AM to 5:59 PM, and the night (ሌሊት) from 6:00 PM to 5:59 AM.
timeConverter.ctaTitle: Your customers think in Habesha time
timeConverter.ctaText: Your booking page can too. {0} shows every slot in Habesha and international time.
timeConverter.cta: Take bookings in Habesha time with {0}
timeConverter.tableCaption: Each international hour in East Africa Time (UTC+3) and the same moment on the Habesha clock.
timeConverter.faq1q: Why does Ethiopian time start at 6 AM?
timeConverter.faq1a: The Habesha clock counts hours from sunrise, not from midnight. Ethiopia is close to the equator, so the sun rises at about 6:00 AM and sets at about 6:00 PM all year. The first hour of the day ends at 7:00 AM, so 7:00 AM is 1 o'clock (ጠዋት 1 ሰዓት) and 6:00 AM is 12 o'clock. The count starts again at sunset: 7:00 PM is 1 o'clock at night.
timeConverter.faq2q: What does 2 o'clock mean in Ethiopian time?
timeConverter.faq2a: It depends on the half of the day. 2:00 in the day (ጠዋት 2 ሰዓት) is 8:00 AM. 2:00 at night (ምሽት 2 ሰዓት) is 8:00 PM. To convert, add 6 hours to the Habesha hour, then use the period word to choose AM or PM.
timeConverter.faq3q: What are day (ቀን) and night (ሌሊት) in Ethiopian time?
timeConverter.faq3a: The Habesha clock has two 12-hour cycles. The day cycle (ቀን) runs from 6:00 AM to 5:59 PM, and the night cycle (ሌሊት) runs from 6:00 PM to 5:59 AM. People usually add a period word: ጠዋት (morning, 6:00 AM to 11:59 AM), ከሰዓት (afternoon, 12:00 PM to 5:59 PM), ምሽት (evening, 6:00 PM to 11:59 PM) and ሌሊት (late night, 12:00 AM to 5:59 AM).
timeConverter.faq4q: Is Ethiopia in a different time zone?
timeConverter.faq4a: No. The Habesha clock is a different way to count the hours, not a different time zone. Ethiopia uses East Africa Time (EAT), which is UTC+3 all year, with no daylight saving time. For example, 3:00 PM EAT in Addis Ababa is 9:00 in Habesha time (ከሰዓት 9 ሰዓት).
timeConverter.faq5q: Which clock do banks, airlines and appointments use?
timeConverter.faq5a: Both clocks are in daily use. Airline schedules, phones and computers show international time (EAT). In conversation, and at many local shops, offices and banks, people use the Habesha clock. When you book or confirm an appointment, say which clock you mean, for example "ጠዋት 3 ሰዓት (9:00 AM)", so nobody arrives six hours early or late.
timeConverter.faq6q: How do I convert Ethiopian time to international time?
timeConverter.faq6a: Add 6 hours to the Habesha hour and keep the minutes. Day hours (ቀን) give a time from 6:00 AM to 5:59 PM, and night hours (ሌሊት) give a time from 6:00 PM to 5:59 AM. For example, ጠዋት 4:30 is 10:30 AM, ምሽት 3:00 is 9:00 PM, and ሌሊት 10:00 is 4:00 AM.

calendar.faq1q: What is today's date in the Ethiopian calendar?
calendar.faq1a: Today's Ethiopian date is shown at the top of this page. It is calculated for Addis Ababa time (UTC+3), so it changes at midnight in Ethiopia. Note that many Ethiopians count the new day from sunrise, not from midnight.
calendar.faq2q: Why is the Ethiopian calendar 7 or 8 years behind?
calendar.faq2a: The Ethiopian Orthodox Church dates the birth of Jesus differently from the Western church. From Meskerem 1 (September) to the end of Tahsas the Ethiopian year is 7 years behind; from January 1 to Pagume it is 8 years behind.
calendar.faq3a: Pagume is the 13th and last month of the Ethiopian year. It has 5 days, or 6 days in a leap year. It falls in early September, just before the new year on Meskerem 1.
calendar.faq4a: Enkutatash is on Meskerem 1. That is 11 September in most years, and 12 September in the year before a Gregorian leap year, because Pagume then has 6 days.
calendar.faq5q: How do Ethiopian leap years work?
calendar.faq5a: Every fourth year Pagume gets a sixth day. An Ethiopian year is a leap year when the year leaves a remainder of 3 when divided by 4, for example 2011, 2015 and 2019. The years are named after the four evangelists: Matthew, Mark, Luke and John, and the leap year is the year of Luke.
calendar.faq6a: Genna is on 7 January in the Gregorian calendar. In the Ethiopian calendar that is Tahsas 29, or Tahsas 28 in the year after a leap year.

reminder.name: Amharic appointment reminder generator
reminder.summary: Ready reminder messages in Amharic and English for SMS, Telegram and WhatsApp.
reminder.title: Amharic Appointment Reminder Message Generator
reminder.description: Write appointment reminders in Amharic and English for SMS, Telegram or WhatsApp, in Habesha or international time, with an SMS length count.
reminder.lede: Fill in the appointment once and get a polite reminder in Amharic and in English, ready to copy or send. Fewer customers forget, and fewer arrive at the wrong hour.
reminder.unicodeNote: Amharic letters use Unicode SMS: 70 characters fit in one SMS, and longer messages are split into parts of 67.
reminder.ctaText: {0} sends an Amharic or English reminder by SMS and email before every booking, in Habesha or international time.
reminder.faq1q: How many characters fit in one Amharic SMS?
reminder.faq1a: An SMS with Amharic (Ethiopic) letters is sent as Unicode, so one SMS holds 70 characters. A longer message is split into parts of 67 characters each, and each part is charged as one SMS. An English-only SMS holds 160 characters.
reminder.faq2q: When should I send an appointment reminder?
reminder.faq2a: Send one reminder the day before the appointment, and a short second one two or three hours before. A reminder sent too early is easy to forget; one sent too late gives the customer no time to change plans.
reminder.faq3q: Should I write the time in Habesha or international time?
reminder.faq3a: Use the clock your customers use. In Amharic, most people expect Habesha time, such as ጠዋት 3:00 ሰዓት. When you choose international time, the Amharic message also shows the Habesha time in brackets, so nobody arrives six hours early or late.
reminder.faq4q: Can I send these messages on Telegram or WhatsApp?
reminder.faq4a: Yes. Choose Telegram or WhatsApp to get a message with short lines, then copy it, or use Share to Telegram to pick the chat. Telegram and WhatsApp messages are not limited to 70 characters.
reminder.faq5a: No. The messages are made in your browser. Nothing you type is sent to a server or saved.

hoursSign.faq1a: Many customers read 2:30 as Habesha time (8:30 AM), others as international time. Showing both clocks on the sign removes the doubt, so nobody comes six hours early or finds the door closed.

hoursSign.faq3q: Which paper size should I print?
hoursSign.faq3a: A4 is good for a door or a window. A5 is good for a counter or a small frame. The layout is the same; the printer scales it to the page.
